mainTopic: The ברכות of מוסף on ראש השנה: where מלכיות and קדושת היום go, when the שופר is blown, and how many פסוקים, and which ones, are said in מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.
overview: This amud opens with the last line of the previous discussion, about one of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות. Then a new משנה gives the order of the nine ברכות of מוסף on ראש השנה. רבי יוחנן בן נורי joins מלכיות to קדושת השם with no שופר. רבי עקיבא joins it to קדושת היום and blows the שופר there. A ברייתא then brings פסוקים as sources for the ברכות, and gives two sources for saying מלכיות. רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree about which ברכה קדושת היום goes with. A story from אושא shows that the custom of יבנה was to blow the שופר for מלכיות. A second משנה requires ten פסוקים in each section, and the גמרא explains what the number ten corresponds to. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי that three פסוקים per ברכה, one each from תורה, נביאים, and כתובים, is enough. The amud ends with a new משנה: no פסוקים about punishment, and the order of the פסוקים.

steps.title: Closing line of the previous discussion on the ordinances
steps.stepSummary: The previous סוגיא ends: a תקנה first said by a student was set in place by his teacher, so it is counted under the teacher's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: And his teacher established it in his name.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the final line of the previous discussion, which carried over onto this page. It explains why a certain תקנה is counted among רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ordinances.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea started with a student. His teacher, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, formally made it binding. That is why it is listed among the teacher's תקנות. Once this line is done, the topic changes completely.

keyTerms.meaning: He established it / fixed it as binding

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the previous סוגיא, not to the משנה that follows. Do not try to connect it to the order of the ברכות.

phrases.english: And his teacher established it in his name.
phrases.notes: Ends the count of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ordinances from the previous daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A תקנה set in place by the teacher is counted as the teacher's ordinance.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order of the blessings
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the order of מוסף on ראש השנה. מלכיות is joined to קדושת השם with no blowing, and the שופר is blown after קדושת היום, זכרונות, and שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The order of the blessings: one says אבות, גבורות, and קדושת השם, and includes מלכיות with them, and does not blow. Then קדושת היום and he blows, זכרונות and he blows, שופרות and he blows. Then he says עבודה, הודאה, and ברכת כהנים. These are the words of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out the full order of the מוסף ברכות on ראש השנה according to רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three ברכות and the last three are the usual ones said all year. The special part is in the middle. רבי יוחנן בן נורי attaches מלכיות to the third ברכה, קדושת השם, and the שופר is not blown there. Blowing happens only after קדושת היום, זכרונות, and שופרות.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה of God's Kingship, built from פסוקים on that theme
The ברכה built from פסוקים that mention the שופר
The ברכה about the holiness of the day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up קדושת השם (the third ברכה, about God's holiness) with קדושת היום (the middle ברכה, about the day's holiness). The whole מחלוקת is about which one מלכיות is attached to.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The order of the blessings:
phrases.notes: Of the מוסף prayer on ראש השנה.

phrases.english: One says Patriarchs, Mighty Deeds, and Sanctification of the Name,
phrases.notes: The usual first three ברכות of every עמידה.

phrases.english: and he includes Kingship with them,
phrases.notes: Meaning joined to קדושת השם.

phrases.english: and he does not blow.
phrases.notes: No שופר after מלכיות.

phrases.english: Sanctification of the Day, and he blows;
Remembrances, and he blows;
Shofarot, and he blows;
and he says Service, Thanksgiving, and the Priestly Blessing,
phrases.notes: The usual last three ברכות.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A brand-new topic. The new משנה has no link to step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, מלכיות is joined to קדושת השם without blowing. The שופר is blown after קדושת היום, זכרונות, and שופרות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא asks why Kingship is said without blowing
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי יוחנן בן נורי: if the שופר is not blown for מלכיות, what is the point of mentioning it?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: If he does not blow for מלכיות, why does he mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא attacks רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order. He is setting up his own alternative order, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא assumes that מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות belong together as a set, each one paired with blowing the שופר. Saying מלכיות with no blowing breaks that pattern and seems to have no purpose. The question is worded as a question, but it works as a challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who disagrees with רבי יוחנן בן נורי

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If he does not blow for Kingship,
why does he mention it?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אִם אֵינוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לְמַלְכִיּוֹת לָמָה הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order given by רבי יוחנן בן נורי in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's placement of מלכיות without blowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלכיות is supposed to be paired with blowing, like זכרונות and שופרות. Saying it without blowing makes no sense.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's order: Kingship joined to the holiness of the day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives his own order. מלכיות is joined to קדושת היום, and the שופר is blown there, so all three special themes are followed by blowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: one says אבות, גבורות, and קדושת השם, and includes מלכיות with קדושת היום and blows; זכרונות and blows; שופרות and blows; and says עבודה, הודאה, and ברכת כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his alternative order. He moves מלכיות from קדושת השם to קדושת היום, where the שופר is blown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only change is where מלכיות sits. Under רבי עקיבא, each of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות is followed by blowing, which solves the problem he raised in step 3. The total is still nine ברכות.
steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions have nine ברכות. רבי יוחנן בן נורי joins מלכיות to קדושת השם, with no blowing. רבי עקיבא joins it to קדושת היום, with blowing.
steps.whyThisMatters: Our מוסף of ראש השנה follows רבי עקיבא. מלכיות is combined with קדושת היום, and the שופר is blown after it.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אוֹמֵר אָבוֹת וּגְבוּרוֹת וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם,
phrases.english: Rather: one says Patriarchs, Mighty Deeds, and Sanctification of the Name,

phrases.aramaic: וְכוֹלֵל מַלְכִיּוֹת עִם קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם וְתוֹקֵעַ,
phrases.english: and includes Kingship with Sanctification of the Day, and blows;
phrases.notes: This is the key change from רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: Remembrances, and blows;
Shofarot, and blows;
and says Service, Thanksgiving, and the Priestly Blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אוֹמֵר אָבוֹת וּגְבוּרוֹת וּקְדוּשַּׁת הַשֵּׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי עקיבא's own order, which fixes the problem he raised in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, מלכיות is joined to קדושת היום with blowing. The שופר is blown after מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.

steps.title: The גמרא quotes רבי עקיבא's question from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by quoting רבי עקיבא's words from the משנה so it can examine them.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי עקיבא said to him: If he does not blow for Kingship, why does he mention it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats רבי עקיבא's line from the משנה word for word. This is a setup: the גמרא is about to question what these words really mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, this line was רבי עקיבא's challenge to רבי יוחנן בן נורי. Here the גמרא quotes it again for a new purpose: to test whether the question makes sense as worded.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA
Rabbi Akiva said to him:
If he does not blow (the shofar) for Kingship —
why does he mention it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם אֵינוֹ תּוֹקֵעַ לְמַלְכִיּוֹת לָמָה הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the משנה's challenge (Step 3) so the גמרא can analyze it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא asks why מלכיות is mentioned if no שופר is blown for it.

steps.title: The תורה commands mentioning Kingship anyway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: how can רבי עקיבא ask why we mention מלכיות, when the תורה tells us to mention it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he mention it?! The Merciful One said: mention it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא's question as worded. Saying מלכיות is a command, so 'why mention it' cannot be a real question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that mentioning מלכיות does not depend on blowing שופר. It is its own requirement from the תורה. So רבי עקיבא's question cannot mean what it seems to say on the surface.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not attacking רבי עקיבא's opinion. It is saying his words cannot be read literally, and it is about to reinterpret them.

phrases.english: Why does he mention it?!
The Merciful One said: mention it!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָה הוּא מַזְכִּיר רַחֲמָנָא אָמַר אַידְכַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal meaning of the quoted question
steps.kashyaTarget: The literal wording of רבי עקיבא's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Mentioning מלכיות is a commandment of its own, so asking why it is mentioned makes no sense.

steps.title: The real question is why Kingship needs ten verses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא really meant: why say a full ten פסוקים for מלכיות? Since it is already different (no שופר), let it be different and have only nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: why ten? Let him say nine, since it is already different, let it be different!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct reading of רבי עקיבא's question. He was not asking whether to say מלכיות at all. He was asking why it gets the same ten פסוקים as the other sections.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן בן נורי, מלכיות already differs from זכרונות and שופרות because no שופר is blown for it. רבי עקיבא's argument is: if it is different in one way, it should be different in its number of פסוקים too. Since everyone says ten for it, it should be treated like the others and get תקיעות as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Ten (the ten פסוקים said in each section)
Since it changed, let it change (fully)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's question is about the number of פסוקים, not about whether to mention מלכיות. Since מלכיות gets ten פסוקים like the others, it should also get שופר blowing like the others.

phrases.english: Rather: why ten (verses)?
Let him say nine,
for since it is already different, let it be different!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by reinterpreting the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא was asking why מלכיות is mentioned at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא was asking why מלכיות gets ten פסוקים if it is already different by having no שופר blowing.

steps.title: Verses behind the first three blessings of שמונה עשרה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings פסוקים from תהלים כ״ט as the sources for the ברכות of אבות, גבורות, and קדושת השם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: From where do we know to say אבות? As it says: 'Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty.' From where do we know to say גבורות? As it says: 'Give to ה׳ honor and strength.' From where do we know to say קדושות? As it says: 'Give to ה׳ the honor of His Name; bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. It gives a source פסוק for each of the first three ברכות of the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק matches one ברכה. 'Sons of the mighty' refers to the אבות. 'Honor and strength' refers to ה׳'s גבורות. 'The honor of His Name' and 'holiness' refer to קדושת השם. This sets up the next question: where do the special ראש השנה ברכות come from?

keyTerms.meaning: The first ברכה of the עמידה, about the Patriarchs
The second ברכה, about ה׳'s mighty deeds
The third ברכה, about ה׳'s holiness

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that we say (the blessing of) Patriarchs —
as it says: 'Give to ה׳, sons of the mighty.'
phrases.notes: תהלים כ״ט:א — the 'mighty' are the אבות

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we say (the blessing of) Mighty Deeds —
as it says: 'Give to ה׳ honor and strength.'
And from where do we know that we say (the blessing of) Holiness —
as it says: 'Give to ה׳ the honor of His Name,
bow to ה׳ in the beauty of holiness.'
phrases.notes: תהלים כ״ט:ב

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the sources for the ברכות of the עמידה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבות, גבורות, and קדושת השם are each learned from a phrase in תהלים כ״ט.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר reads the ראש השנה verse
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות. רבי אליעזר reads ״שבתון זכרון תרועה מקרא קדש״ phrase by phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know to say מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות? רבי אליעזר says: As it is written, 'a solemn rest, a remembrance of blowing, a holy gathering.' 'Solemn rest' is קדושת היום; 'remembrance' is זכרונות; 'blowing' is שופרות; 'holy gathering' means make it holy by (refraining from) doing work.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves on to the special ברכות of ראש השנה. רבי אליעזר matches each word of the ראש השנה פסוק in ויקרא to a part of the day's davening or to a law of the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר, the first word, שבתון, is the source for קדושת היום. The last phrase, מקרא קדש, teaches the ban on מלאכה. Notice that this reading gives sources for זכרונות and שופרות but does not yet give a word for מלכיות.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה about the holiness of the day

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we say Kingship, Remembrances, and Shofaros —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
For it is written: 'a solemn rest, a remembrance of blowing, a holy gathering.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״ג:כ״ד

phrases.english: 'Solemn rest' — this is the Holiness of the Day;
'Remembrance' — these are Remembrances;
'Blowing' — these are Shofaros;
'Holy gathering' — make it holy regarding doing work.
phrases.notes: That is, by not doing forbidden work

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאוֹמְרִים מַלְכִיּוֹת זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the regular ברכות to the special ראש השנה ברכות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבתון means קדושת היום, זכרון means זכרונות, תרועה means שופרות, and מקרא קדש means not doing מלאכה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the opening word should mean resting
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי אליעזר: why not say that שבתון, the first word, teaches resting from work?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Why don't we say 'solemn rest' means resting, since that is what the verse opened with first?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא objects to how רבי אליעזר matched the first word. He argues that שבתון should mean resting from work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שבתון literally sounds like rest (שבות). It also comes first in the פסוק, and the main point of a יום טוב is that work is forbidden. So רבי עקיבא thinks the ban on מלאכה belongs to שבתון, not to מקרא קדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
For what reason should we not say
'solemn rest' — (means) resting,
since the verse opened with it first!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֹאמַר שַׁבָּתוֹן שְׁבוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אליעזר's reading of שבתון
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading of שבתון as קדושת היום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שבתון sounds like rest and comes first, and the most basic law of the day is resting, so it should teach the ban on work.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's own reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא gives his reading: שבתון teaches resting from work, זכרון means זכרונות, תרועה means שופרות, and מקרא קדש means קדושת היום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: 'solemn rest' means make it holy regarding doing work; 'remembrance' is זכרונות; 'blowing' is שופרות; 'holy gathering' is קדושת היום.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא offers his own word-by-word reading. He switches the meanings of the first and last phrases compared to רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that זכרון means זכרונות and תרועה means שופרות. They disagree only on which phrase teaches the ban on work and which teaches קדושת היום. For רבי עקיבא, שבתון teaches the ban on work and מקרא קדש teaches קדושת היום.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: שבתון = קדושת היום, and מקרא קדש = no מלאכה. רבי עקיבא: שבתון = no מלאכה, and מקרא קדש = קדושת היום. Both agree on זכרון = זכרונות and תרועה = שופרות.

phrases.english: Rather: 'solemn rest' — make it holy regarding doing work;
'Remembrance' — these are Remembrances;
'Blowing' — these are Shofaros;
'Holy gathering' — this is the Holiness of the Day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge, רבי עקיבא gives his own alternative reading
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שבתון means not doing מלאכה, and מקרא קדש means קדושת היום. זכרון and תרועה stay the same as in רבי אליעזר's reading.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מלכיות must be said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of saying מלכיות, since neither רבי אליעזר's nor רבי עקיבא's reading of the פסוק covered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that we say מלכיות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. Both readings of the פסוק gave sources for זכרונות and שופרות, but neither gave one for מלכיות. This line sets up the answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר used שבתון for קדושת היום and מקרא קדש for resting from work. רבי עקיבא swapped those two. Either way, all four phrases are used up and none is left for מלכיות. That leaves a gap: where does the requirement to say מלכיות come from? The next two steps give two different sources.

keyTerms.meaning: From where (do we learn this)? It asks for a source.
The ברכה and פסוקים about ה׳ as King

phrases.english: From where is it derived that we say Kingship verses?
phrases.notes: This fills the gap left by רבי עקיבא's reading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the readings of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, neither of which gave a source for מלכיות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that teaches the requirement to say מלכיות on ראש השנה.

steps.title: רבי learns מלכיות from neighboring פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי points out that ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ appears right before the ראש השנה section, ״בחדש השביעי״. This teaches that we mention ה׳'s kingship on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: The Torah says ״I am ה׳ your God,״ and right after that it says ״In the seventh month.״ This is מלכות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי answers the question. The words ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״, which speak about ה׳'s rule, are placed right next to the ראש השנה פסוקים. So we must mention His kingship on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ ends ויקרא 23:22, and ״בחדש השביעי״ (the ראש השנה section) starts two פסוקים later. Because the two are placed next to each other (a סמיכות), we read them together. ה׳'s kingship belongs on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
"I am ה׳ your God": a phrase about ה׳'s rule over us
"In the seventh month": the opening of the ראש השנה section

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: רבי means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: "I am the Lord your God" (Leviticus 23:22)
phrases.notes: This is the end of the פסוק about gifts to the poor.

phrases.english: and "In the seventh month" follows it. This is Kingship.
phrases.notes: Because the two are placed side by side, kingship is linked to ראש השנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מלכיות comes from ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ being placed next to ״בחדש השביעי״.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר יהודה gives a different source: kingship goes wherever there are זכרונות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says רבי's proof is not needed. A פסוק in במדבר speaks of זכרון and then adds an extra ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״. This teaches that wherever there are זכרונות, there must also be מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: That is not needed. The Torah says ״They shall be a remembrance for you before your God.״ There was no need for the Torah to add ״I am ה׳ your God.״ So why does it say ״I am ה׳ your God״? This sets up a general rule (בנה אב) for every place where זכרונות are said: מלכיות must go with them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר יהודה offers a different source for מלכיות. He points to an extra phrase in במדבר 10:10, which links kingship to remembrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק already says ״לפני אלהיכם״ ("before your God"), so adding ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ seems unnecessary. Since it is extra, it teaches something new: kingship must always go with remembrance. So wherever זכרונות are required, as on ראש השנה, מלכיות are required too.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed. The proof brought before is unnecessary.
There was no need for the פסוק to say this. This marks an extra phrase that must be teaching something.
Built a general rule (a model case that applies everywhere)
The ברכה and פסוקים about ה׳ remembering

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why מלכיות and זכרונות are treated as a pair. The same פסוק also mentions blowing the trumpets, so all three themes appear together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
This is not necessary, for the verse says:
"And they shall be to you for a remembrance before your God" (Numbers 10:10)
phrases.notes: The phrase "before your God" already mentions God.

phrases.english: for there was no need for the verse to say "I am the Lord your God"
so why does the verse say "I am the Lord your God"?
This builds a general rule for every place
where Remembrances are mentioned:
Kingship verses should be with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the need for רבי's proof and offers a different source for מלכיות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever זכרונות are said, מלכיות must be said with them. This is learned from the extra ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ in במדבר 10:10.

steps.title: Which ברכה should קדושת היום go with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the special ראש השנה ברכות should include קדושת היום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where does one say קדושת היום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the order of the ברכות. It sets up a disagreement between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ראש השנה, the middle of the מוסף already has three special themes: מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות. קדושת היום, the ברכה about the holiness of the day, must also be said. Since there is no separate ברכה for it, the question is which theme it joins.

keyTerms.meaning: The ברכה about the holiness of the day
And where does one say it?

phrases.english: And where does one say the Sanctification of the Day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of sources and turns to the order of the ברכות, a topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה קדושת היום should be combined with.

steps.title: רבי: קדושת היום goes with מלכיות, as the fourth ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי says קדושת היום is said together with מלכיות. Everywhere else, קדושת היום is the fourth ברכה, so here too it should be fourth.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says: One says it with מלכיות. Just as we find everywhere that it is in the fourth ברכה, so too here it is in the fourth ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives his answer. He places קדושת היום in the fourth ברכה, joined with מלכיות, to match its usual spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת and יום טוב, קדושת היום always comes right after the first three ברכות, making it the fourth. On ראש השנה, מלכיות is the fourth ברכה. So רבי combines קדושת היום with מלכיות to keep it in its usual fourth place.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we find. This compares the case to the usual pattern.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: Rabbi says:
One says it with the Kingship blessing.
Just as we find everywhere that it is in the fourth blessing,
phrases.notes: For example, on שבת and יום טוב.

phrases.english: so too here, it is in the fourth.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: עִם הַמַּלְכִיּוֹת אוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קדושת היום goes with מלכיות as the fourth ברכה, matching every other davening.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: קדושת היום goes with זכרונות, in the middle ברכה
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says קדושת היום is said together with זכרונות. Everywhere else, it is the middle ברכה, so here too it should be in the middle, the fifth of nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: One says it with זכרונות. Just as we find everywhere that it is in the middle, so too here it is in the middle.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with רבי. He places קדושת היום in the middle ברכה, which on ראש השנה is זכרונות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them follow the usual pattern of davening, but each sees that pattern differently. רבי says the rule is "fourth." רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the rule is "middle": on שבת, the fourth of seven ברכות is the middle one. ראש השנה מוסף has nine ברכות, so the middle one is the fifth, which is זכרונות.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with רבי here

steps.confusionAlert: On שבת, "fourth" and "middle" are the same ברכה, so it is easy to think רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agree. They only differ on ראש השנה. There are nine ברכות, so the middle one is the fifth (זכרונות), not the fourth (מלכיות).
steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources for מלכיות: רבי learns it from the פסוקים placed side by side in ויקרא, and רבי יוסי בר יהודה learns it from the extra ״אני ה׳ אלהיכם״ in במדבר. There are also two placements for קדושת היום: רבי puts it with מלכיות (the fourth ברכה), and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל puts it with זכרונות (the middle ברכה). Our נוסח combines קדושת היום with מלכיות.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One says it with the Remembrances blessing.
Just as we find everywhere that it is in the middle,
phrases.notes: On שבת it is the fourth of seven, which is the middle.

phrases.english: so too here, it is in the middle.
phrases.notes: Here that means the fifth of nine.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת אוֹמְרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי's placement by understanding the usual pattern as "middle" rather than "fourth."
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדושת היום is said with זכרונות, the middle (fifth) of the nine ברכות.

steps.title: In אושא, the first prayer leader follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי and is corrected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא tells that in אושא, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא led the prayers following רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל told him that this was not the custom in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the בית דין set the year in אושא, רבי יוחנן בן ברוקא went down to lead the prayers in front of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He followed the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי. רבן שמעון said to him: 'This is not how they used to do it in יבנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing how the ראש השנה ברכות were actually said. The first שליח ציבור used רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל objected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי puts מלכיות into the third ברכה, קדושת השם, and does not blow the שופר for it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rejected this by pointing to the established custom of יבנה. The story moves the debate from theory into real practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Usha, a town in the Galil where the סנהדרין met after יבנה
Went down before (the תיבה), meaning he led the prayers as שליח ציבור
Used to practice; the established custom
Yavne, the earlier seat of the סנהדרין, whose custom carried authority
Set the year or month officially, here referring to ראש השנה

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: And when the court sanctified the year in Usha,
Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka went down (to lead the prayers)
phrases.notes: 'Going down' refers to the prayer leader's spot, which was lower than the rest of the shul.

phrases.english: in front of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
and he acted like Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.
phrases.notes: He included Kingship in the third blessing (Sanctification of God's Name).

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon said to him:
They did not used to do it this way in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בֵּית דִּין אֶת הַשָּׁנָה בְּאוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא about the placement of the ראש השנה ברכות by showing what happened in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's order, with מלכיות inside קדושת השם, was not the practice of יבנה.

steps.title: The second prayer leader follows רבי עקיבא and is approved
steps.stepSummary: On 'the second day', רבי חנינא, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, led the prayers following רבי עקיבא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that this was the custom in יבנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day, רבי חנינא, the son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, went down to lead the prayers and followed רבי עקיבא. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: 'This is how they used to do it in יבנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with a second שליח ציבור who followed רבי עקיבא, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved. This approval sets up both of the next questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא puts מלכיות together with קדושת היום and blows the שופר for it. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's approval seems to mean he fully agrees with רבי עקיבא. The גמרא will soon question that.

keyTerms.meaning: On the second day; its exact meaning is discussed later

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
keyTerms.meaning: The second prayer leader in the story

phrases.english: On the second day, there went down (to lead)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina, the son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
and he acted like Rabbi Akiva.
phrases.notes: He put Kingship together with Sanctification of the Day and blew the shofar.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
This is how they used to do it in Yavne.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי יָרַד רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story by contrasting the second prayer leader with the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא's practice matched the custom of יבנה, according to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: How can רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approve רבי עקיבא's order?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really agrees with רבי עקיבא. They argue about which ברכה קדושת היום goes with.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds like רבי עקיבא? But רבי עקיבא said to say מלכיות together with קדושת היום, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said to say קדושת היום together with זכרונות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's approval seems to contradict his own opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that קדושת היום goes in the middle, with זכרונות. רבי עקיבא puts it with מלכיות. So why would רבן שמעון בן גמליאל praise a שליח ציבור who followed רבי עקיבא?

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? A formula introducing a surprising implication
But didn't he say? A formula introducing a contradiction

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two arguments here. One argument is about where מלכיות goes and whether the שופר is blown for it (רבי יוחנן בן נורי versus רבי עקיבא). The other argument is about where קדושת היום goes (רבי עקיבא versus רבן שמעון בן גמליאל).

phrases.english: Is that to say that Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
holds like Rabbi Akiva?
But didn't Rabbi Akiva say:

phrases.aramaic: מַלְכִיּוֹת עִם קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם אָמַר לְהוּ,
phrases.english: one says Kingship together with Sanctification of the Day,
and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: קְדוּשַּׁת הַיּוֹם עִם הַזִּכְרוֹנוֹת אָמַר לְהוּ?
phrases.english: one says Sanctification of the Day together with Remembrances?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's approval in the story seems to imply.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's approval of רבי עקיבא's practice in the story.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's own opinion puts קדושת היום with זכרונות, not with מלכיות. So he should not approve רבי עקיבא's order.

steps.title: He agreed only about blowing the shofar for Kingship
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved only one part of רבי עקיבא's practice: blowing the שופר for מלכיות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: He meant to say that we blow the שופר for מלכיות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל did not agree with everything רבי עקיבא does. He agreed only that the שופר is blown for מלכיות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי does not blow the שופר for מלכיות, but רבי עקיבא does. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved רבי עקיבא's practice on that point alone. He still disagrees about where קדושת היום goes.

keyTerms.meaning: To say; he meant to teach

steps.whatToRemember: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'this is how they did it in יבנה' was a partial approval. He agreed with blowing the שופר for מלכיות, not with רבי עקיבא's placement of קדושת היום.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
He meant to say that we blow the shofar for Kingship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: לוֹמַר שֶׁתּוֹקְעִין לְמַלְכִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agreed to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the approval
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agreed with all of רבי עקיבא's practice, including where קדושת היום goes.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agreed only that the שופר is blown for מלכיות, against רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

steps.title: What does 'the second day' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's words 'on the second day' and asks what they mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: 'On the second day רבי חנינא went down to lead.' What is 'the second'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the story and asks what it means. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Second day' could mean the second day of the same ראש השנה, or something else. The גמרא needs to define it before it can understand the story.

keyTerms.meaning: What? What is the meaning of?

phrases.english: 'On the second day, Rabbi Chanina went down (to lead).'
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the baraita again in order to explain it.

phrases.english: What is 'second'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the content of the story to a question about its wording.

steps.title: It cannot mean the second day of יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: If it meant the second day of יום טוב, then אלול would have been made a 30-day month. But since עזרא's time, אלול was never made full.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the second day of יום טוב, that would mean they made אלול a full month! But רבי חנינא בר כהנא said: From the days of עזרא onward, we never found אלול made full!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the simple reading, 'the second day of יום טוב', and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There would only be a 'second day' if אלול had 30 days, so that the 30th of אלול was treated as the first day and the 1st of תשרי became the second day. But רבי חנינא בר כהנא testifies that אלול was never made full after עזרא. So this reading does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggestion that will be rejected

phrases.english: If you say it means the second day of the Festival,
is that to say that they made Elul a full month?!
But didn't Rabbi Chanina bar Kahana say:
From the days of Ezra onward
we have not found Elul made full!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי — לְמֵימְרָא דְּעַבְּרוּהּ לֶאֱלוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes the simplest meaning of 'second day' and attacks it.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading 'second day' as the second day of יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading requires a 30-day אלול, which never happened after עזרא.

steps.title: 'Second' means the following year's ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that 'the second day' means the next ראש השנה, a year later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What does 'second' mean? The second time, on ראש השנה of the following year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the correct meaning: the second story happened on ראש השנה one year later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This avoids the problem of a 30-day אלול. The two prayer leaders led on two different years' ראש השנה, both in אושא in front of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who explains the ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The two prayer leaders in אושא led on two different years. The story shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל approved blowing the שופר for מלכיות.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is 'second'? On the second day (time),
in the following year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי שֵׁנִי — לְיוֹם שֵׁנִי, לַשָּׁנָה הַבָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty by giving a different meaning of 'second'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Second day' meant the second day of the same ראש השנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Second day' means ראש השנה of the following year.

steps.title: New משנה: at least ten verses for each section
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that at least ten פסוקים are said in each of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not say fewer than ten פסוקים of מלכיות, ten of זכרונות, and ten of שופרות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the minimum number of פסוקים for each special ראש השנה ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about the order and placement of the ברכות. Now the topic changes to their content: each section needs at least ten פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not go below; the minimum is

phrases.english: MISHNA:
We do not say fewer than ten verses of Kingship,
than ten of Remembrances,
than ten of Shofarot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The topic moves from the order of the ברכות to how many פסוקים each one has.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At least ten פסוקים must be said for each of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: three verses each is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says that if someone said only three פסוקים for each section, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: If he said three of each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dissenting opinion. רבי יוחנן בן נורי holds that three פסוקים per section is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion requires ten פסוקים for each section. רבי יוחנן בן נורי lowers the minimum to three for each. The word 'יצא' suggests that three works after the fact, even if more is better.

keyTerms.meaning: From all of them, meaning each section

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
If he said three of each of them,
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: אִם אָמַר שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ מִכּוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about the minimum number of פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות, and שופרות is enough to fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: What do the ten Kingship verses correspond to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the number ten in the משנה's requirement of ten פסוקים of מלכיות is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: These ten verses of Kingship, what do they correspond to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking where the number ten comes from. This question sets up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה required at least ten פסוקים for each section but never explained why ten. The גמרא wants a source or parallel that gives this number meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The section of מוסף on ראש השנה about ה׳'s Kingship

phrases.english: GEMARA: These ten Kingship verses
to what do they correspond?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the משנה's rule of ten פסוקים from step 25 and asks for its basis.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or parallel behind the number ten.

steps.title: רבי: the ten praises of David
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the ten פסוקים match ten praises that דוד said in ספר תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said: They correspond to the ten praises that דוד said in the book of תהלים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives the first answer: the ten פסוקים parallel ten praises of ה׳ written by דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number ten is tied to a set of ten praises in תהלים. The answer does not yet say which praises are meant, and that gap leads directly to the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi said:
Corresponding to the ten praises
that David said in the book of Psalms.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים correspond to ten praises of דוד in תהלים.

steps.title: There are many more praises than ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ספר תהלים contains far more than ten praises.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are many praises in תהלים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי: ספר תהלים is full of praises, so why does he speak of exactly ten?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'praises' means all the praises in תהלים, the count is far above ten and the parallel falls apart. רבי's answer only works if he is pointing to one specific group of praises.

phrases.english: There are many praises!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count in רבי's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תהלים has far more than ten praises, so the number ten does not fit.

steps.title: Specifically the praises in the shofar chapter
steps.stepSummary: רבי means the praises in the chapter that says 'הללוהו בתקע שופר', which has ten calls to praise ('הללו אל' and nine times 'הללוהו').
steps.simpleTranslation: He means those praises in the place where it is written 'Praise Him with the blast of the שופר'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי was referring to one specific chapter, the last chapter of תהלים, which contains exactly ten calls to praise ('הללו אל' and nine times 'הללוהו').
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is resolved by narrowing 'praises' to the ten calls to praise in that one chapter. This chapter also mentions שופר, which makes it a fitting parallel for ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: With the blast of the שופר

phrases.english: Those in which it is written
"Praise Him with the blast of the shofar."
phrases.notes: תהלים 150, which contains ten calls to praise ('הללו אל' plus nine 'הללוהו')

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי against the challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All the praises in תהלים, which number far more than ten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the ten calls to praise in the שופר chapter.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a link between the ten פסוקים and a chapter that itself mentions שופר, which is fitting for ראש השנה.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the Ten Commandments
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the ten פסוקים correspond to the עשרת הדברות given to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They correspond to the Ten Commandments that were said to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף offers a second, different source for the number ten: the עשרת הדברות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is an alternative parallel, not a response to רבי. It links the פסוקים to the giving of the תורה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Corresponding to the Ten Commandments
that were said to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים correspond to the עשרת הדברות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the ten utterances of Creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ten פסוקים correspond to the ten מאמרות through which the world was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They correspond to the ten utterances through which the world was created.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן offers a third source for the number ten: the ten statements ה׳ used to create the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This parallel fits ראש השנה, the day that marks the creation of the world. As with רבי's answer, the גמרא will now ask which ten utterances are meant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Corresponding to the ten utterances
through which the world was created.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּנֶגֶד עֲשָׂרָה מַאֲמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third answer to the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten פסוקים correspond to the ten מאמרות of Creation.

steps.title: Which are the ten utterances?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ten utterances רבי יוחנן means.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which are they?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear list of the ten utterances. This sets up the answer and the challenge that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'ten utterances' needs to be matched to actual words in the תורה. Only then can the count of ten be checked.

phrases.english: Which are they?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the details of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ten utterances of Creation are meant.

steps.title: The times it says 'And He said'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is the occurrences of 'ויאמר' in the story of Creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The times it says 'And He said'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies the utterances as the places in the Creation story where the תורה writes 'ויאמר אלקים'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'ויאמר' marks an act of Creation done through speech. Whether these really add up to ten is checked in the next step.

phrases.english: "And He said" —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ten utterances are the instances of 'ויאמר' in the Creation story.

steps.title: There are only nine 'And He said'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that 'ויאמר' appears only nine times in the Creation story, not ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are only nine times 'And He said' in בראשית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counts the times 'ויאמר' appears and finds only nine, which does not match רבי יוחנן's ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The identification in step 34 now seems to come up one short. Unless a tenth utterance can be found, רבי יוחנן's parallel fails.

phrases.english: The "And He said" of Genesis
are nine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count given in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that there are ten utterances
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting 'ויאמר' gives only nine, not ten.

steps.title: 'In the beginning' is also an utterance
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בראשית' also counts as an utterance, as the פסוק says 'בדבר ה׳ שמים נעשו'. That makes ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'In the beginning' is also an utterance, as it is written: 'By the word of ה׳ the heavens were made.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the first act of Creation, 'בראשית ברא', was also done through speech, even though the word 'ויאמר' does not appear there. That brings the total to ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק in תהלים says the heavens were made by ה׳'s word. This shows that the opening creation of 'heaven and earth' was itself an utterance, so 9 + 1 = 10.

keyTerms.meaning: In the beginning (the first act of Creation)
By the word of ה׳ the heavens were made

steps.whatToRemember: There are three opinions on the source of the ten פסוקים: רבי says the ten praises in the שופר chapter of תהלים, רב יוסף says the עשרת הדברות, and רבי יוחנן says the ten מאמרות of Creation, which are nine 'ויאמר' plus 'בראשית'.

phrases.english: "In the beginning" is also an utterance,
as it is written: "By the word of the Lord the heavens were made."
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:6

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the counting problem raised in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a hidden item to the count, supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בראשית' is also an utterance, giving ten.

steps.title: What does 'three of each' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי's ruling and asks whether he means three from each of תורה, נביאים and כתובים (nine total), or one from each (three total).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: If he said three of each, he has fulfilled his obligation. A question was asked: What is he teaching? Three from the תורה, three from the נביאים, and three from the כתובים, making nine, so the difference between him and the תנא קמא is just one? Or perhaps one from the תורה, one from the נביאים, and one from the כתובים, making three, so the difference between them is large?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the next line of the משנה and raises an איבעיא: what exactly did רבי יוחנן בן נורי mean by 'three'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'שלש שלש' are unclear. They could mean three פסוקים from each of the three parts of תנ״ך, for a total of nine, which is only one less than the תנא קמא's ten. Or they could mean three in total, one from each part, which is seven less than the תנא קמא.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them (a dilemma); here it is resolved in steps 38 and 39
How is he teaching? (what does he mean?)

steps.confusionAlert: At this point 'שלש שלש' is still unclear. It could mean nine in total (three from each part of תנ״ך) or three in total (one from each part). Steps 38–39 settle it as three per ברכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם אָמַר שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁלֹשׁ מִכּוּלָּן — יָצָא.
phrases.english: If he said three of each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation.
A dilemma was raised to them: What is he teaching?

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלֹשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה, שָׁלֹשׁ מִן הַנְּבִיאִים,
phrases.english: Three from the Torah, three from the Prophets,
and three from the Writings —
which make nine,
and the difference between them is one;
or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מִן הַתּוֹרָה, וְאֶחָד מִן הַנְּבִיאִים,
phrases.english: one from the Torah, and one from the Prophets,
and one from the Writings —
which make three,
and the difference between them is a lot?

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: מימרא (for the quoted line of the משנה)
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the number ten and re-quotes רבי יוחנן בן נורי from step 26 in order to clarify his meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'three of each' means nine פסוקים in total or three in total.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer decides the minimum number of פסוקים needed in each section of מוסף on ראש השנה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: ten verses each, but seven is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to settle the question. The first opinion says one should say ten פסוקים for each of מלכיות, זכרונות and שופרות, but seven is acceptable after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: One should not say fewer than ten Kingship verses, ten Remembrance verses, and ten שופר verses. But if he said seven of each, he has fulfilled his obligation, matching the seven heavens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from Step 37. This first part sets up the background, and the actual proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets the ideal at ten פסוקים per ברכה and the minimum at seven per ברכה. Notice that every number here is counted per ברכה. That helps us read רבי יוחנן בן נורי's number the same way in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to settle a question

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
One does not say fewer than ten Kingship verses,
than ten Remembrance verses, than ten Shofar verses,
and if he said seven of each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation,
corresponding to the seven heavens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to resolve the question asked in Step 37
steps.raayaObject: The meaning of רבי יוחנן בן נורי's number of פסוקים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording both the first opinion and רבי יוחנן בן נורי

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: three per ברכה, one from each section
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says the minimum is three for each ברכה, matching תורה, נביאים and כתובים, or alternatively כהנים, לוים and ישראלים. This shows he means one פסוק from each section, three in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי said: someone who says fewer than ten should not go below seven. But if he said three of each, he has fulfilled his obligation, matching תורה, נביאים and כתובים. Some say: matching כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the answer to Step 37. רבי יוחנן בן נורי's minimum is three פסוקים for each ברכה, which means one from each section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן נורי first says 'one who goes below ten should not go below seven,' and then adds that three is still enough after the fact. If 'three' meant nine, it would already be above seven, and the added clause would teach nothing. So 'three' must mean three per ברכה. The reason given, matching three groups, fits one פסוק for each group. So the second option in Step 37 is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: one who reduces, who says fewer than ten
and some say: an alternative version
the three groups of the Jewish people

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'three' as three from each section (nine total). It means three per ברכה, one from תורה, one from נביאים and one from כתובים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri said:
One who says fewer than ten should not say fewer than seven,
but if he said three of each of them, he has fulfilled his obligation,
corresponding to Torah, Prophets and Writings,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: כְּנֶגֶד כֹּהֲנִים לְוִיִּם וְיִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: and some say: corresponding to Kohanim, Levi'im and Yisraelim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and supplies the proof
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן נורי means nine פסוקים or three per ברכה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Three per ברכה, one from each of תורה, נביאים and כתובים

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא in the name of שמואל rules like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה is like רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on this topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ideally one says ten פסוקים per ברכה. However, the halachic minimum after the fact is three, one from each section of תנ"ך.
steps.whatToRemember: Ideally ten פסוקים per ברכה. The הלכה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי that three per ברכה, one each from תורה, נביאים and כתובים, is enough after the fact.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said in the name of Shmuel:
The halacha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules on the dispute just quoted
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like רבי יוחנן בן נורי: the minimum is three פסוקים per ברכה.

steps.title: New משנה: no verses about punishment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that one may not use זכרונות, מלכיות or שופרות verses whose theme is punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One does not mention Remembrance, Kingship or שופר verses that speak about punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules out using any פסוק whose theme is punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we discussed how many פסוקים to say. Now the משנה limits which פסוקים may be chosen: they must not be about punishment, even if they contain the right key word.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One does not mention Remembrance, Kingship and Shofar verses
that are about punishment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַזְכִּירִין זִכָּרוֹן מַלְכוּת וְשׁוֹפָר שֶׁל פּוּרְעָנוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on the content of the פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פסוקים about punishment may not be used in מלכיות, זכרונות or שופרות.

steps.title: Start with תורה and end with נביאים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets the order: begin with פסוקים from the תורה and finish with a פסוק from נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He begins with the תורה and concludes with the נביא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the order in which the פסוקים are said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order matches the order of תנ"ך: the תורה comes first. The last פסוק should come from נביאים.

phrases.english: He begins with the Torah and concludes with the Prophet,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the order of the פסוקים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוקים start with תורה and end with נביאים.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: ending with תורה is also valid
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says that if one ended with a פסוק from the תורה, he has still fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: if he concluded with the תורה, he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי disagrees with the first opinion of the משנה about the closing פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion wants the last פסוק to come from נביאים. רבי יוסי says ending with a תורה פסוק also works, at least after the fact.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
If he concluded with the Torah, he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אִם הִשְׁלִים בַּתּוֹרָה — יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion's rule about how to conclude
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ending with a פסוק from the תורה is valid.
